articles.description: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered Earth's atmosphere after 22 years in orbit, ending its mission. Swift was crucial for understanding gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic events, detecting over 2,000 bursts. The spacecraft's orbit deteriorated due to increased solar activity, leading to its uncontrolled descent. NASA attempted a rescue operation, but it ultimately failed, resulting in its re-entry on November 4, 2026.

articles.title: Filipino engineer wins £30,000 award for sensor that detects hidden earthquake damage in buildings
articles.description: A Filipino structural engineer has won the 2026 James Dyson Global Sustainability Award and £30,000 for developing Sentinel, a sensor that detects hidden damage in buildings after earthquakes. The invention could help engineers assess potentially unsafe buildings more quickly and reduce the risk of collapse.

articles.title: Fireworks on Dalal Street: BSE Sensex soars 1,400 points, NSE Nifty50 gains 2%
articles.full_text: For a point of reference, the Nifty 50 closed near 24,300 on Diwali 2024. By Diwali 2025, the index had climbed to roughly 25,700, delivering a steady return of nearly 5.7% over that period. More importantly, valuations have become significantly cheaper as earnings have grown. On Diwali 2024, the Nifty 50 traded at a Price-to-Earnings (PE) ratio of around 22.5. Today, heading into Diwali 2026, the present market PE ratio has moderated to a highly attractive 19.1, making Indian equities a compelling value proposition.Despite this fundamental strength, investors must adapt to shifting market mechanics. As long as global interest rates remain elevated, broad-based index rallies will be constrained. We are firmly in a stock picker's market. Moving forward, a rigorous, bottom-up approach is essential. The market consistently rewards companies with strong earnings, agnostic to global anxieties. Stock market today: Investors gain over Rs 6.9 lakh crore - why Dalal Street is rallying The market rally extended beyond the benchmark indices, with mid-cap and small-cap stocks also joining the party. The Nifty Midcap 100 climbed 1.46%, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 1.49%. The Nifty 100 also advanced 1.78%. Among sectoral indices, Nifty Private Bank led the gains with a 2.55% rise, followed by Nifty Realty at 1.92%. Nifty IT advanced 1.72%, Nifty Auto gained 1.66%, Nifty Consumer Durables rose 1.52% and Nifty Media climbed 1.36%. Nifty FMCG also ended 1.08% higher. The renewed participation of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) added to the market's strength. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said, "Foreign institutional investors have returned as significant buyers, the revival in overseas fund flows marks an encouraging development for domestic equities, particularly as sustained institutional participation could lend greater depth to the ongoing market recovery" Equity benchmarks continued their winning run on Thursday, with BSE Sensex surging 1,510.81 points, or 1.95%, to 78,812.21. NSE Nifty 50 also climbed 423.20 points, or 1.77%, to 24,344.10. According to Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, "The sharp advance reflects improving global risk sentiment, supported by lower crude prices and renewed institutional buying. However, the ability of the benchmarks to sustain these gains beyond the opening trades will be crucial in determining whether the positive momentum can translate into a broader upward move. Crude oil prices have retreated sharply; the decline offers some relief to an oil-import-dependent economy such as India". Stock market today: Top stocks to buy on November 5 Equity benchmarks might be headed for a positive opening on Thursday, tracking the sharp decline in international crude oil prices and gains across global markets. GIFT Nifty futures stood at 24,295.5, indicating a higher start for the Nifty 50, which had closed at 23,960.6 in the previous session. Brent crude futures declined another 1% to $93.5 per barrel after falling 8.7% in the previous session. The correction followed the US midterm election outcome, with investors assessing whether the Democrats' victory could accelerate efforts to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. Foreign fund flows remained another important domestic market factor. Provisional data showed that foreign investors purchased Indian shares worth Rs 72.84 billion ($769.65 million) on Wednesday. This marked their fourth consecutive session of buying, indicating a return of foreign participation following a substantial sell-off in Indian equities earlier in the year. Asian equities advanced, tracking gains on Wall Street after the US midterm election results, with a Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress coinciding with a sharp correction in crude oil prices. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.3%, supported by gains in benchmark indexes across Japan and Australia. The broader regional advance followed a strong session in the US. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%, marking its biggest single-session gain in three months, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.9%. South Korea moved in the opposite direction, with the Kospi Index declining 2.7%. Investor concerns surrounding the future of data-centre development and losses in US semiconductor stocks weighed on the benchmark. US Treasuries extended their gains amid optimism that lower oil prices could help contain inflation. The dollar weakened for a second consecutive day, while US oil futures held on to their declines in early Thursday trade after Brent crude had fallen more than 8% in the previous session. Treasuries also gained across the yield curve as investors reduced bets on Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes over the coming year. The dollar recorded its steepest decline in two months. International crude oil prices witnessed a sharp correction following the US midterm election results, with both Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures falling below the $100-per-barrel mark. Brent crude declined $9.27, or 8.9%, to $94.29 a barrel, touching its lowest level since September 4. US WTI futures dropped $7.44, or 7.8%, to $88.54. However, industry executives cautioned that the decline in prices may not necessarily translate into a sustained easing, as US President Donald Trump's weakened political position could complicate efforts to end the Iran war. Democrats' control of Congress could constrain funding for the conflict, while Trump may seek to demonstrate strength by intensifying military operations against Tehran. Executives said an escalation involving ground forces could prolong the conflict, disrupt energy supplies and raise costs for consumers. A decisive outcome, whether through military action or a negotiated deal, was considered preferable to a prolonged stalemate that continues to weigh heavily on oil importers. Rupee ended Wednesday's session with modest gains against the US dollar, supported by a weaker greenback and lower crude oil prices. The  currency settled at 94.64 per dollar, compared with its previous close of 94.74, as investors assessed the implications of the US midterm election results. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of six major currencies, declined 0.4% to 101.3. The euro, sterling and Swiss franc were among the currencies registering gains against the greenback. Rupee had touched a two-week high during early trade but subsequently pared some of its gains as importer and interbank dollar bids gathered strength around the 94.50 mark. Stock market extended its winning streak for the fifth consecutive session on Wednesday, with the Sensex climbing nearly 384 points to close above the 77,000 mark. Buying in blue-chip financial, FMCG and automobile stocks, continued foreign fund inflows and easing crude oil prices supported the rally. The BSE Sensex gained 384 points to settle at 77,301, its highest closing level in more than two months. During the session, the index had surged as much as 478 points to touch 77,396. The five-session rally has added more than 4,000 points, or 5%, to the benchmark. The NSE Nifty also advanced 150 points to close at 23,961. Among Sensex constituents, Bharat Electronics, Titan, InterGlobe Aviation, Bajaj Finance, ITC and Adani Ports emerged as the biggest gainers. On the other hand, Tata Consultancy Services, HCL Tech, Infosys and Eternal were among the laggards. Foreign institutional investors purchased equities worth Rs 6,837 crore on Tuesday, according to exchange data. Brent crude, meanwhile, declined 0.7% to $102.8 per barrel. Market participants also pointed to improving global sentiment following the US midterm election outcome, which raised expectations of a more measured approach to trade and tariff policies and potentially stronger foreign fund flows into emerging markets. Mid- and small-cap stocks also extended their outperformance amid improving risk appetite.

articles.title: Ramayana Movie Review and Release Live Updates
articles.full_text: Another viewer shared a detailed reaction after watching the film in IMAX 3D on a real IMAX screen. The review described the experience as visually breathtaking and praised the scale of the production. "What a breathtaking visual spectacle! 🙏Never in my wildest dreams did I imagine Indian cinema pulling off something on this scale, with jaw dropping visuals and exhilarating action sequences! Not all early reactions focused on criticism. One enthusiastic viewer gave the film a strong recommendation and encouraged others to watch it in theatres. "Guys, it gives me great pleasure to tell that that Ramayana is peak. Go watch it." Actor-filmmaker Rishab Shetty also shared his thoughts on the ambitious adaptation. He appreciated the effort to bring an important Indian story and cultural tradition to the big screen. "There's something truly special about seeing our timeless stories and culture brought to life on such a grand scale. A proud moment for Indian cinema!" The reviewer also reflected on how the story of the 'Ramayana' has been presented to audiences over the years. The epic has remained familiar to generations through family storytelling and television adaptations. "Ramayana has always been a part of our growing-up years. We’ve heard the story in so many different ways  from our grandmother telling us their Excerpts from the Ramayana saga, the iconic television serial, and more recently, infamous Om Raut’s Adipurush. The viewer recalled initially wondering whether the project would simply become another expensive adaptation. The involvement of Namit Malhotra and his association with DNEG Studios had also shaped those expectations. "So when Namit Malhotra announced Ramayana, our initial thought was, okay, this guy owns DNEG Studios, so perhaps he’s just attempting another lavish, big-budget adaptation." Despite those initial doubts, the viewer was pleasantly surprised by the film's execution. The review offered an encouraging assessment of the adaptation and its treatment of the epic. "But surprisingly, the adaptation is very good!"
